results.title: Revamped supply chain strategies can help mitigate tariff impacts
results.content:
Operational changes: strategic partnerships, risk management, and automation

Adding tariff clauses to supplier agreements is now standard practice for 45 percent of organizations. Among our respondents, dynamic pricing models (40 percent) and financial hedging strategies (39 percent) are also gaining traction, reflecting a shift toward embedding risk controls and flexibility directly into commercial relationships. [...] Only a small minority (18 percent) maintain their current export regimes. Our respondents’ most common strategies include reconfiguring supply chains (62 percent), adjusting export pricing and product mix (61 percent), and diversifying export markets (48 percent). [...] Strategic logistics partnerships (64 percent) and tariff cost-sharing agreements (61 percent) are the most sought-after alliances. Manufacturing joint ventures in low-tariff regions are also popular (38 percent), as companies look to optimize supply chains and share the financial burden of tariffs.
